messages.subject: measurement invariance and ordered variables
parts:
Hi,

i used the measurementinvariance() function from semTools for a cfa-model with ordered observed variables and found that the chi-square decreases, e.g. when going from constrained loadings to constrained loadings and intercepts. when i use the ml-estimator, chi-square increases with each additional constrained, and i would expect the same under the WLS-approach.

I guess, i need to adapt the constraints? were could i find information on this?

best wishes!

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance and ordered variables
parts:
With *robust* versions of both ML and WLS, chi-square difference tests are not so straightforward.  With these robust options, the reported chi-square has been adjusted or scaled.  To find a chi-square difference, one must first un-adjust the two reported values, calculate the difference and then adjust the difference.  Check the statistic that is being reported--is it a straight WLS or a robust WLS?
--Ed Rigdon

The best way to study this is fit the two models one by one, and use the
anova() function to get the (scaled) chi-square difference test.

There is not a lot of literature on the behaviour of the scaled
chi-square difference test in the context of ordinal data...

Yves.

Perhaps I should give some more information:

by default, if a scaled test statistic has been used (for both models),
the anova() function uses the (original) formulas from Satorra (2000)
(references below) to compute a correct 'scaled' test statistic (a
scaled chi-square difference test). Not easy to compute (and it may
fail), but you always get a positive test statistic.

You can also use the (currently undocumented) option SB.classic=TRUE, as in

anova(fit1, fit2, SB.classic=TRUE)

which will use the well-known approximate formulas from Satorra &
Bentler (2001). which are easy to compute (even by hand), but may lead
to a negative test statistic now and then. These are the formulas from
the Mplus website.

In dev 0.5-16, there is a new function 'lavTestLRT()' which has all this
properly documented.

References:

Satorra, A. (2000). Scaled and adjusted restricted tests in
multi-sample analysis of moment structures. In Heijmans, R.D.H.,
Pollock, D.S.G. & Satorra, A. (eds.), Innovations in multivariate
statistical analysis. A Festschrift for Heinz Neudecker
(pp.233-247). London: Kluwer Academic Publishers.

Satorra, A., & Bentler, P. M. (2001). A scaled difference
chi-square test statistic for moment structure analysis.
Psychometrika, 66(4), 507-514.


Yves
